section_summary: This section documents State Department and occupation-authority procedures for entering Japan, including application forms, diplomatic circulars, acknowledgments, military clearances, and discussions of travel by businessmen, missionaries, officials, and family members. A major group concerns revised rules for admitting missionaries and the applications of Colombian, Spanish, and Irish nuns. Other cases involve Indian and Iranian merchants, a Burmese reparations representative, an Austrian woman seeking reunion with her Japanese husband, Chinese travelers in transit, and New Zealand claimants seeking property in Japan.

subfiles.title: Application by H. Ismil to Visit Japan
subfiles.to: Director, Office of Control, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests permission to inspect the welfare of Indian merchant personnel remaining in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ismil proposes a ten-day visit to Tokyo and Kobe before returning to India through China.

subfiles.title: Personal-Baggage License for Japanese Nationals
subfiles.from: John C. Borton, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Edward E. Hunt, Department of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that an existing general license covers the baggage of Japanese nationals who are not internees or deportees.
subfiles.summary: Commerce sees no need to notify customs collectors because the current personal-baggage license is adequate.

subfiles.title: Circular Note on Form DS-513 and Travel to Japan, Second Copy
subfiles.to: Chiefs of Mission of governments not represented in Japan
subfiles.about: Introduces Form DS-513 for routing applications for military permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Missions should complete applications in triplicate, retain one copy, and forward two to the Special Projects Division. A distribution list identifies governments receiving the circular.

subfiles.title: Circular Note on Form DS-513 and Travel to Japan, Duplicate Copy
subfiles.to: Chiefs of Mission of governments not represented in Japan
subfiles.about: Supplies application forms and instructions for seeking military permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Applications should be prepared in triplicate and routed through the Special Projects Division to military authorities in Japan.

subfiles.title: Form DS-513: Application for Permission to Enter Japan
subfiles.about: Blank form requesting personal, passport, itinerary, occupational, and travel-purpose information.
subfiles.summary: Blank standardized application for civilian permission to enter occupied Japan.

subfiles.title: Theater Clearance for Eugenio Rubino
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Reports theater clearance for Italian diplomatic secretary Eugenio Rubino.
subfiles.summary: A military permit would issue upon application, although a note reports Rubino was already in Japan.

subfiles.title: No-Yong Park's Request for Help Obtaining Japan and Korea Permits
subfiles.about: Asks for assistance securing military permission to visit Japan and Korea during a trip to China.
subfiles.summary: Park explains his Chinese nationality, reentry arrangements, and Senator Barkley's efforts to obtain the required permits.

subfiles.title: Advice to No-Yong Park on Far Eastern Travel
subfiles.about: Advises Park to consult the Passport Division about documents and permits for Far Eastern travel.
subfiles.summary: Stelle offers to discuss Park's plans if he visits Washington.

subfiles.title: Promotional Brochure for No-Yong Park
subfiles.about: Advertises No-Yong Park's background, publications, lecture subjects, and endorsements.
subfiles.summary: The brochure portrays Park as an accomplished Chinese scholar and popular interpreter of Asian affairs. It lists his education, books, lecture topics, testimonials, and speaking-management contact.

subfiles.title: Stelle's Reply Regarding Park's Permit Request
subfiles.about: Explains that Park's permit request is already before the appropriate authorities.
subfiles.summary: Stelle says he cannot assist further and hopes Park's request and trip prove successful.

subfiles.title: File Charge Card for George Fujii Correspondence
subfiles.about: Records circulation of correspondence concerning George Fujii.
subfiles.summary: File charge card for the Fujii travel-permit correspondence.

subfiles.title: Request for Forms for George Fujii's Visit to Japan
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests forms and procedural guidance for George Fujii's proposed trip to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kashiwa describes Fujii as an American citizen of Japanese ancestry and a leading Honolulu merchant.

subfiles.title: Reply Concerning George Fujii's Proposed Business Trip
subfiles.about: Explains that private businessmen cannot yet enter Japan but restrictions are expected to ease.
subfiles.summary: Fujii should await a public announcement, then apply through the Passport Division or appropriate Hawaiian authorities.

subfiles.title: Broadened Regulations for Entry of Missionaries into Japan
subfiles.to: War Department for the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Sets revised conditions governing entry, support, dependents, supplies, and transportation of missionaries.
subfiles.summary: Missionaries require assurances of shelter, support, qualifications, and freedom from dependence on occupation resources. The policy permits limited dependents and supply shipments, restricts Army assistance to emergencies, and allows exceptional short visits by senior church officials.

subfiles.title: Statement of Conditions for Missionary Entry into Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes shelter, food, language, shipment, and support requirements for missionaries entering Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mission organizations must provide inspected housing and adequate food and clothing. Army support is reimbursable and exceptional; preference goes to experienced or Japanese-speaking missionaries, while unusual cases receive individual review.

subfiles.title: Latvian Acknowledgment of April 24 Circular
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the circular and forms concerning permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Latvian Minister acknowledges receipt of the revised application procedure.

subfiles.title: Lebanese Acknowledgment of Japan Travel Forms
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the April 24 circular and enclosed applications for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lebanon confirms receipt of the modified military-permission procedure and forms.

subfiles.title: Uruguayan Acknowledgment of Japan Entry Information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges information about obtaining permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Uruguay confirms receipt of the April 24 circular note.

subfiles.title: Colombian Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the travel-permit procedure and ten sets of Form DS-513.
subfiles.summary: Colombia confirms receipt of the circular and application sets.

subfiles.title: Syrian Acknowledgment of Japan Travel Circular
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the April 24 circular and reports forwarding it to Syria.
subfiles.summary: Syria confirms receipt and transmission of the travel forms to its government.

subfiles.title: Airgram Regarding Adrienne Franziska Wada
subfiles.about: Reports referral of Wada's request to the appropriate military authorities.
subfiles.summary: The consul will be informed when military authorities decide whether Wada may enter Japan.

subfiles.title: Application for Entry to Japan of Adrienne Wada
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Batavia
subfiles.about: Transmits Wada's application to join her Japanese husband in Tokyo with their son.
subfiles.summary: Austrian-born Adrienne Wada was interned pending repatriation to Germany. The Batavia Red Cross urged rapid approval so she and her son could instead establish their home with Professor Saichi Wada in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Draft Airgram Regarding Adrienne Wada
subfiles.about: Drafts notice that Wada's case has been referred to military authorities.
subfiles.summary: Promises to report the military decision on Wada's requested travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Internal Review Questions Concerning Mrs. Wada
subfiles.about: Raises questions about Wada's internment, Austrian involvement, and her husband's identity.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg suggests letting authorities in Japan investigate Professor Wada if the request is referred to the military.

subfiles.title: File Search for Adrienne Franziska Wada
subfiles.about: Records negative searches for information concerning Adrienne Franziska Wada.
subfiles.summary: Several State Department offices found no information concerning Wada.

subfiles.title: Referral of Wada Entry Request to Colonel Lynch
subfiles.about: Asks military authorities to consider Wada's request for permanent entry with her son.
subfiles.summary: Chappell summarizes Wada's nationality, internment, family, destination, and Red Cross support, asking to be advised of military action.

subfiles.title: Telegram Reporting Habib Ordoubadi's Travel Application
subfiles.about: Reports an Iranian merchant representative's request to visit Japanese cotton-manufacturing areas.
subfiles.summary: Habib Ordoubadi seeks a two-month Japanese buying and selling trip beginning in July.

subfiles.title: Reply on Habib Ordoubadi's Proposed Business Trip
subfiles.about: Says Ordoubadi applied through the wrong channel and private business travel remains barred.
subfiles.summary: Ordoubadi should await the expected announcement easing restrictions on private business travel.

subfiles.title: El Salvador Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the circular, application sets, and procedure for military permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: El Salvador transmitted the information to its government and expressed appreciation.

subfiles.title: Honduran Acknowledgment of Japan Entry Procedure
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the revised military-permission procedure and its transmission to Honduran authorities.
subfiles.summary: Honduras confirms receipt and referral of the travel information.

subfiles.title: Panamanian Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges ten sets of Form DS-513 for prospective travelers to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Panama thanks the Secretary for the circular and forms.

subfiles.title: State Member Memorandum on Interchange of Persons with Japan
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State Member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Opposes a permanent policy bar on educational and scientific visits despite Japan's temporary shortages.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring argues that scholarly interchange would reduce Japan's cultural isolation and support democratization. The attached proposed statement says visits may be delayed temporarily but deserve high priority when economic and housing conditions improve.

subfiles.title: Alternate Copy of State Member Memorandum on Interchange
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State Member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Restates State's objections to making temporary travel limitations permanent policy.
subfiles.summary: Advocates priority for educational and scientific travel once food and housing permit.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary Draft of State Member Memorandum
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State Member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Drafts the State position favoring eventual scholarly and scientific interchange with Japan.
subfiles.summary: A fragmentary copy rejects a temporary-condition amendment and supports resuming visits when economic conditions improve.

subfiles.title: File Search for U Tun Ohn
subfiles.about: Records negative file searches concerning U Tun Ohn.
subfiles.summary: FC and ES reported no information about U Tun Ohn.

subfiles.title: Telegram Requesting Entry Permit for U Tun Ohn
subfiles.about: Urgently requests Japanese entry clearance for Burma's reparations and restitution representative.
subfiles.summary: U Tun Ohn planned four months in Tokyo as a Commonwealth mission member and hoped to depart May 20.

subfiles.title: Conversation About U Tun Ohn's Mission Status
subfiles.about: Clarifies that U Tun Ohn must be accredited to the British reparations mission.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Eichler confirmed that SCAP invited FEC governments and that the British mission could include the Burmese representative.

subfiles.title: Instructions for Routing U Tun Ohn's Application
subfiles.about: Directs that Ohn's application be routed through the British representative in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: As a British subject, Ohn should apply through the British reparations mission under SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Finnish Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the circular and forms for military permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Finland confirms that the filing instructions have been noted.

subfiles.title: Finnish Acknowledgment of Form DS-513, Duplicate
subfiles.about: Duplicate acknowledgment of the circular and Japan travel forms.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of Finland's acknowledgment and acceptance of the filing instructions.

subfiles.title: Approval for Six Nuns to Enter Japan
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP approval for six nuns and explains passport endorsements and baggage allowances.
subfiles.summary: Five Colombian and one Spanish nun may enter Japan with reasonable baggage after appropriate passport statements are added.

subfiles.title: Interim Reply on Six Missionary Applications
subfiles.about: Reports that six applications are being forwarded and SCAP's decision will follow.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy will receive SCAP's decision after military review.

subfiles.title: Conversation About Missionaries' Personal Effects
subfiles.about: Clarifies limits on personal effects and food carried by missionaries entering Japan.
subfiles.summary: Colonel Linville allowed reasonable personal effects for personal use and up to one ton of food.

subfiles.title: Despatch Transmitting Six Nuns' Applications
subfiles.from: Margaret Parr Hays, American Vice Consul, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Transmits six missionary nuns' applications for prompt referral to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The Worshipper nuns seek early entry into Japan, where their community had operated before the war.

subfiles.title: Application of Julia Isaza Jaramillo
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests indefinite entry into Japan as a Colombian missionary nun.
subfiles.summary: Application cites convent housing and 25 kilograms of personal effects.

subfiles.title: Application of María de Jesús Aguilar Gómez
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests clearance to enter Japan as a missionary nun.
subfiles.summary: Partially illegible application for the second Colombian Worshipper nun.

subfiles.title: Application of María Isabel Bohórquez Morales
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests indefinite entry into Japan as a Colombian missionary nun.
subfiles.summary: Application lists Yokohama convent housing and 25 kilograms of effects.

subfiles.title: Application of María del Carmen Prieto Agudelo
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests entry into Japan for indefinite convent service.
subfiles.summary: Application proposes travel from Bogotá through Miami and San Francisco to Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Application of Josefina Ocampo Castaño
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests indefinite entry into Japan as a Colombian missionary nun.
subfiles.summary: Application identifies Yokohama housing, sponsorship, and 25 kilograms of personal effects.

subfiles.title: Application of María Cruz de la Rosa
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests entry into Japan as a Spanish missionary nun.
subfiles.summary: Application proposes indefinite convent service in Yokohama and 25 kilograms of effects.

subfiles.title: File Search for Six Missionary Nuns
subfiles.about: Records negative file searches for the six Colombian and Spanish applicants.
subfiles.summary: FC, VD, and ES found no information concerning any applicant.

subfiles.title: Referral of Six Nuns' Applications to Commander Millett
subfiles.about: Forwards six missionary applications and requests a decision on entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard identifies the applicants, corrects their likely point of origin to Bogotá, notes their requested personal effects, and asks whether they may proceed.

subfiles.title: Nicaraguan Acknowledgment of April 24 Circular
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the circular and Form DS-513 copies for prospective travelers.
subfiles.summary: Nicaragua confirms receipt of the Japan entry procedure and forms.

subfiles.title: Siamese Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Form DS-513 and reports its transmission to Siamese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Siam confirms receipt and forwarding of the application form.

subfiles.title: Request to Extend Permissions for Six Irish Nuns
subfiles.about: Requests extensions so six Irish nuns can reach Japan before the end of June.
subfiles.summary: The nuns planned to sail from Cobh to New York aboard the Marine Flasher before continuing to Japan.

subfiles.title: Trade Timing When Private Businessmen Enter Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Suggests delaying private export-import transactions after foreign businessmen are first admitted.
subfiles.summary: The proposed delay would prevent established firms from gaining an unfair advantage and allow publication of available commodities.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Extending Irish Nuns' Permissions
subfiles.about: Records Irish travel plans and a request to extend six military permissions.
subfiles.summary: The nuns expected a month-long journey from New York to Japan; Wolberg requested written confirmation before seeking extensions.

subfiles.title: Request to Millett for Extensions for Six Irish Nuns
subfiles.about: Requests extensions of six Irish nuns' expiring clearances for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Their proposed voyage would outlast the original sixty-day permissions.

subfiles.title: Cuban Acknowledgment of Form DS-513
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the April 24 circular and ten sets of travel application forms.
subfiles.summary: Cuba notes the information governing individual travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Dominican Acknowledgment of Japan Travel Procedure
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the April 24 procedure for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The information was transmitted to the appropriate Dominican authorities.

subfiles.title: Denial of the Sturts' Proposed Visit to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports military rejection of the Sturts' visit and suggests remote recovery of missing property.
subfiles.summary: Travel was denied because Japan lacked billeting and messing facilities and approval could invite many similar requests. Reginald Sturt was advised to send property details to the Civil Property Custodian for investigation and possible return through the British delegation.

subfiles.title: Nicaraguan Acknowledgment of Exit-Permit Waiver
subfiles.about: Acknowledges waiver of American exit permits for most foreign nationals cleared to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The waiver excludes German and Japanese nationals and requires evidence of SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Extension of Irish Nuns' Clearances to July 15
subfiles.about: Clarifies the expiration date and documentation for six Irish nuns' extended clearances.
subfiles.summary: Commander Millett confirmed that all six permissions remained valid through July 15, 1947. He also accepted one Irish memorandum covering the entire group rather than separate statements.

subfiles.title: Request for Transit Permit for Mei Li Tong Chen and Children
subfiles.about: Requests a military transit permit for a mother and two children flying to China through Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Mei Li Tong Chen and her children would remain only while their Northwest Airlines plane refueled.

subfiles.title: JCS Approval of Extensions for Six Irish Nuns
subfiles.from: John R. Millett, Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: States no objection to extending the six Irish nuns' Japan clearances.
subfiles.summary: The Military Permit Section approves the requested extensions.

subfiles.title: Notice to Ireland of Extended Permissions
subfiles.about: Notifies Ireland that six nuns' permissions were extended through July 15, 1947.
subfiles.summary: The Military Permit Secretary extended each nun's authorization to enter Japan.
